title: Bash Tool 300s Hard Timeout Requires Restart
summary: The bash tool forcibly times out around 300 seconds with 'timed out: bash has not returned in 300.0 seconds and must be restarted', killing the command and requiring a tool restart.
implications: Long-running commands beyond ~300s are terminated and lose stdout/stderr.
Wrappers sharing the same bash session can require a restart to proceed.
Extended workflows can be interrupted mid-task if a single step overruns.
mitigations: Keep commands under 300s; split large tasks into smaller units.
Use `timeout 290s <cmd>` to control failure points and cleanup.
Persist progress to disk between steps and use file-based polling for backgrounded work (`<cmd> &`).
Write checkpoints/progress logs to files so runs can be resumed after timeouts.
recovery: Restart the bash tool (call with restart: true) and rerun a short validation command before resuming.
